stories.start_quote: מעשה באדם אחד שהי׳ זהיר במצות ציצית
stories.summary_en: Talmudic tale (Menahot 44a), retold as part of a homily: a man careful with tzitzit goes to a costly harlot overseas, but his four fringes strike him in the face and he withdraws from the sin. The homilist uses it to explain why a bride sends the groom a tallit.

tags.why: the talmudic tale is embedded in a homily explaining a wedding custom and a verse
illicit sex with a harlot; the homily ties it to the verse on adultery

quotes: ואף הוא עלה וישב ערום כנגדה
tags.why: his desire for the harlot drives the plot

quotes: באו ארבע ציצותיו וטפחו לו על פניו נשמט
tags.why: he withdraws from the sin at the last moment
the tale turns on avoiding a forbidden act

quotes: באו ארבע ציצותיו וטפחו לו על פניו
tags.why: the fringes strike him, a quasi-miraculous event

quotes: שולחת לו טלית עם ד׳ ציצית
tags.why: the tallit and tzitzit carry religious significance

quotes: ביום שנכנס לחופה עם בת זוגו
tags.why: the homily's frame concerns the wedding custom
the harlot is the second main character

missing_concepts: tzitzit as a commandment that protects from sin
wedding custom of the bride sending a tallit
